slides.texte_overlay:
How to make people
respect you without
raising your voice
Say no without a speech. "I can't this weekend." That's it. No three excuses, no long apology. People respect a clear no way more than a yes you obviously didn't mean.
Do what you said you'd do. Every time, small things too. Respect isn't built in one big dramatic moment. It's built by being the guy whose word is never a maybe, week after week.
Don't gossip. When someone starts trashing a person who isn't there, don't join in. Change the subject or stay quiet. People notice, and they trust the guy who won't talk about them either.
Know what you're talking about. Five minutes a day of history, art or science adds up fast. People respect someone who actually knows things, not the guy who just talks the loudest.
slides.texte_sophia: Know what you're talking about. Swap five minutes of scrolling for a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science, every day. People respect a guy who actually knows things.

slides.texte_overlay: Set your boundaries early and calmly. "I don't mind helping, but I need a heads-up next time." Said once, without anger, it sticks. Waiting until you explode just makes you look out of control.
Carry yourself well in public. Sit up straight, put the phone away, give people your full attention when they talk. How you carry yourself tells people how to treat you before you say a word.
Stay calm when someone tries to wind you up. Breathe out, drop your shoulders, answer in your normal voice. "Interesting take." The guy who can't be provoked always has the most control in the room.
